article.title: Measuring Customer Movement Properly: Cohorts, Transition Rates, and Value Migration
article.why: Track how the same customers move across value states instead of relying on static tier counts.

paragraphs.en:
A membership program can look successful if the number of top-tier customers increases from one year to the next. But that snapshot does not tell us whether existing customers actually moved upward, whether new customers entered at high value, or whether the tier thresholds changed. To understand customer development, analysts need to track movement, not just year-end population counts.

The first step is to define a cohort. Choose a fixed set of customers at a starting point and follow the same people through time. For example, take all active members as of December 2025 and observe their 2026 tier. This avoids mixing customer movement with acquisition and attrition. If the total number of Gold members rises, a cohort view can show whether that happened because Silver members upgraded, new customers joined as Gold, or low-value customers left the base.

A transition matrix is one of the most useful tools. Rows represent the starting tier and columns represent the ending tier. Each cell shows the share or number of customers who moved from one state to another. The diagonal captures stability. Cells above the diagonal show upward movement; cells below show downgrades. A separate inactive state can capture customers who disappeared.

Transition rates are more informative than raw counts because tier populations can differ greatly in size. If 20,000 Silver customers move to Gold out of 200,000 Silver members, the upgrade rate is 10 percent. If 5,000 Gold customers move to Platinum out of 20,000 Gold members, the upgrade rate is 25 percent. Raw movement counts and transition probabilities answer different questions.

However, even transition rates can be distorted if tier definitions change. Suppose the Gold threshold falls from 500,000 yen to 400,000 yen. More customers will appear to move upward even if their spending is unchanged. For year-over-year analysis, analysts should either hold definitions constant or explicitly separate rule-induced movement from behavior-induced movement.

Value migration goes beyond rank labels. A customer may stay in the same tier but increase annual spending from 520,000 to 690,000 yen. Another may remain Gold while dropping from 690,000 to 510,000 yen. Both are ‘stable’ in the transition matrix, yet one relationship strengthens while the other weakens. Tracking spending change within tiers adds a continuous view of movement.

Net migration can also be useful. For each tier, analysts can compare inflows from lower tiers, outflows to higher tiers, downgrades, and exits. A tier may grow even while many existing members deteriorate if enough new customers enter. Without decomposing flows, the ending population can hide this churn.

Cohort retention should be linked to movement as well. Customers who disappear from the program are not merely missing observations. They represent a transition to inactivity or exit. If analysts calculate only movements among customers who remain active, they create survivorship bias and make the system look healthier than it is.

Another important distinction is between nominal and real value. Inflation or price increases can push spending upward without a meaningful increase in purchase volume or engagement. If tier thresholds remain fixed, more customers may upgrade mechanically. Depending on the business, analysts may need to examine purchase frequency, units, or inflation-adjusted spending to interpret migration correctly.

Time horizon matters. Monthly transitions can be noisy because customers naturally fluctuate around thresholds. Annual transitions may be too slow to detect early deterioration. Many programs benefit from using both: short-term movement indicators for monitoring and annual qualification outcomes for formal tier decisions.

Segment analysis can reveal where mobility differs. Younger customers may upgrade quickly but also churn more. Families may move gradually but remain stable once upgraded. Customers using multiple payment channels may show stronger upward movement than single-channel users. These differences can inform targeted interventions.

The strongest analysis connects movement to economics. An upgrade is valuable only if it creates durable incremental contribution after accounting for benefit costs. A customer who barely crosses a threshold, receives expensive benefits, and then downgrades next year may be less valuable than a customer who grows steadily without immediate tier change.

A practical dashboard can therefore include starting cohort size, transition matrix, upgrade and downgrade rates, inactive rate, within-tier spending change, net value migration, and post-transition retention. These measures should be calculated under consistent definitions and accompanied by notes when rules change.

The key lesson is that membership value is dynamic. Year-end tier counts describe where customers are, but not how they got there. Cohorts, transition rates, and value migration reveal the path. That path is what managers need if they want to distinguish genuine customer development from population turnover, rule changes, and temporary spending fluctuations.

This framework also improves experimentation. If a promotion targets customers near a tier boundary, success should not be judged only by how many treatment customers end the year in a higher tier. Analysts can compare treatment and control transition matrices, estimate incremental upgrade probability, and measure whether upgraded customers remain valuable afterward. This distinguishes persuasion from natural movement.

It is also useful to separate gross upward movement from net upward movement. Gross movement counts everyone who upgraded. Net movement subtracts downgrades or exits that offset those gains. A program can celebrate 50,000 upgrades while simultaneously experiencing 45,000 downgrades, producing much less improvement than the headline suggests.

Finally, visualizing movement as a flow rather than a stack of bars can change management discussion. A static chart encourages questions about tier size. A transition view encourages questions about causes: which customers are improving, which are deteriorating, where are they coming from, and what action could change the next transition? That shift from stock to flow is essential for managing long-term customer value.
paragraphs.zh:
會員制度如果高 rank 人數比去年增加，看起來很成功，但靜態 snapshot 無法告訴我們既有顧客是否真的升級、新客是否直接以高價值進入、或只是 threshold 改變。要理解 customer development，必須追蹤 movement，而不只看年末各 rank 人數。

第一步是固定 cohort。選定起始時點的一組顧客，跨期追蹤同一批人。例如固定2025年12月 active members，再看他們2026年的 tier。這可避免把 acquisition、attrition 與 customer movement 混在一起。

Transition matrix 是核心工具。Row 是起始 tier，column 是結束 tier；對角線代表維持，上方代表升級，下方代表降級，另加 inactive state 捕捉流失。

Transition rate 比 raw count 更容易比較不同大小 tier。例如20萬 Silver 中2萬升 Gold 是10%，2萬 Gold 中5千升 Platinum 是25%。Raw movement count 與 transition probability 回答不同問題。

若 tier definition 改變，transition 也會被扭曲。例如 Gold threshold 從50萬降到40萬，即使顧客 spending 沒變，也會出現更多「升級」。跨年分析要固定 definition，或明確拆出 rule-induced movement 與 behavior-induced movement。

Value migration 不只看 rank label。同樣留在 Gold，有人從52萬升到69萬，有人從69萬掉到51萬；matrix 都算 stable，但經濟含義完全相反。因此還要看 within-tier spending change。

Net migration 也有用。每個 tier 應拆 inflow、outflow、downgrade、exit。Tier 人數可以增加，同時既有會員卻大量惡化，只要新客進入夠多即可。

Cohort retention 要和 movement 一起看。消失的顧客不是 missing observation，而是 transition to inactive。若只看仍 active 的人，就會有 survivorship bias。

還要區分 nominal 與 real value。Inflation 或 price increase 可以在 engagement 沒改善時推高 spending，若 threshold 固定，就會機械式增加升級。因此可能需要一起看 frequency、units 或 inflation-adjusted spending。

Time horizon 也重要。Monthly transition 容易受 threshold 附近波動干擾，annual transition 又可能太慢；可同時用短期 indicator 做 monitoring、年度 outcome 做正式資格判定。

Segment analysis 能找出不同 mobility pattern，例如 younger customers 升得快但 churn 也高，家庭客成長慢但升級後穩定。

最強的分析要把 movement 接到 economics。Upgrade 只有在扣除 benefit cost 後仍創造 durable incremental contribution 才有價值。

Dashboard 可包含 starting cohort、transition matrix、upgrade/downgrade rate、inactive rate、within-tier spending change、net value migration、post-transition retention。

核心是 membership value 是動態的。Year-end tier counts 只描述顧客在哪裡，cohort、transition rate、value migration 才告訴我們他們怎麼走到那裡。

Experiment 也應比較 treatment/control 的 transition matrix 與 incremental upgrade probability，而不是只看 treated 最後有多少人升級。Gross upward movement 還應和 downgrade/exit 一起看 net movement。把圖從 static stock 改成 flow，也能讓管理層更聚焦於原因與下一步行動。
paragraphs.ja:
membership programでtop-tier人数が増えても、既存顧客が本当にupしたのか、新規顧客が高価値で入ったのか、threshold変更の影響なのかはsnapshotだけでは分かりません。customer developmentを見るにはmovementを追う必要があります。

まずcohortを固定します。2025年12月時点のactive membersなど同じ顧客を2026年まで追えば、acquisitionやattritionとcustomer movementを分けられます。Gold人数増加がSilverからのupgradeなのか、新規Gold流入なのかも区別できます。

transition matrixではrowをstarting tier、columnをending tierにします。対角線はstay、上側はup、下側はdowngrade、inactive stateは離脱を示します。

transition rateはraw countより比較しやすいです。20万Silverのうち2万がGoldなら10％、2万Goldのうち5千がPlatinumなら25％です。countとprobabilityは別の問いに答えます。

ただしtier definition変更には注意します。Gold thresholdを50万円から40万円へ下げればspendingが同じでもupgradeが増えます。year-over-yearではdefinitionを固定するか、rule-induced movementとbehavior-induced movementを分けます。

value migrationはrank label以上の情報を持ちます。同じGoldでも52万円から69万円へ増える顧客と69万円から51万円へ下がる顧客では意味が違います。within-tier spending changeも必要です。

net migrationでは各tierへのinflow、上位へのoutflow、downgrade、exitを分解します。新規流入が多ければtier人数が増えても既存顧客が悪化している場合があります。

cohort retentionではinactiveもtransitionとして扱います。active顧客だけでmatrixを作るとsurvivorship biasが起きます。

inflationやprice increaseによりpurchase volumeが同じでもspendingだけ増えることがあるため、frequency、units、real valueも必要に応じて確認します。

monthly movementはnoiseが多く、annual movementは遅いため、短期monitoringと正式annual qualificationを併用するとよいでしょう。

segment別mobilityも重要です。若年層はupgradeが速いがchurnも高い、family層はゆっくりだが安定する、といった違いが施策設計につながります。

最終的にはmovementをeconomicsへ接続します。benefit costを引いた後もdurable incremental contributionがあるupgradeに価値があります。

dashboardにはstarting cohort、transition matrix、upgrade/downgrade rate、inactive rate、within-tier change、net migration、post-transition retentionを含めます。

重要なのはtier countというstockだけでなくflowを見ることです。experimentでもtreatment/controlのtransition matrixを比較し、natural movementではなくincremental upgradeを測るべきです。

vocabulary.usage: Follow a fixed cohort across years.
Use a transition matrix to track tier movement.

business.term: Year-end tier counts show where customers are; transition analysis shows how they got there.
business.explanation: 區分靜態存量與動態流動。

sources: Cohort analysis, transition matrices, value migration, survivorship bias, and loyalty-tier economics.
